pr_title: [Merged by Bors] - Added example of entity sorting by components
pr_body:
We discussed with @alice-i-cecile privately on iterators and agreed that making a custom ordered iterator over query makes no sense since materialization is required anyway and it's better to reuse existing components or code. Therefore, just adding an example to the documentation as requested.

Fixes #1470.
pr_comments: Since there were large changes and the original code doesn't exist anymore, where should I put the example?
I would include this example as part of docs on [`QueryIter`](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/c78b76bba8def0d72b579b4a06673843f32e8532/crates/bevy_ecs/src/query/iter.rs).

I think including a complicated sort in the query iter doc comments is a bit distracting. It forces users to mentally break down what the sort is doing, which feels pretty tangential to the goal of teaching them how to query for something. Imo using `contains` with a comment explaining why accomplishes the same goal with less headache.
Or alternatively simplify the sort by only sorting a single item, not using reverse, and using `sort_by_key`

issue_context.title: Ordered iteration over Queries
issue_context.body:
**What problem does this solve or what need does it fill?**

Iterating over queries in a particular order is a reasonably common pattern: it is used for a) prioritization and early stopping b) ensuring reproducible execution, particularly when dealing with PRNG or modifying a common piece of data with floating point math.

It can be done manually with the current tools, but they are frustrating to write and read, and hard to optimize.

**What solution would you like?**

Provide a pair of `Query` methods: `ordered_iter` and `ordered_iter_mut`, which iterate over the entities in the query in the specified order.

In the example demonstrating this feature, show how to iterate in `Entity` order, and explain why using `Entity` as your ordering is / isn't stable, because it's the obvious thing to try and that property relies on deep engine internals.

In the example demonstrating this feature, show how to sort your entities by the value of one of their components, then iterate over the query in that order.

**What alternative(s) have you considered?**

Manually implement this functionality in each system using a for loop over the ordering, then using the appropriate `query.get` call.

Manually implement this functionality as a method on `Query` using a trait in each app that needs this functionality.

I'm not a fan of either of these approaches, as a) they create a lot of conceptual overhead and b) getting an optimized iteration method is challenging from the outside.

**Additional context**

The `ordered_iter` crate has a nice reference implementation / [API](https://docs.rs/ordered_iter/0.1.2/ordered_iter/trait.OrderedSetIterator.html) that we can probably borrow from.

This may be efficient to implement at the same time as #762.

It's not immediately clear how / if to combine this with parallel iteration. It's useful in some cases, but nonsensical in others.
comments: Won't it be affected by @cart changes? I would like to give it a try.

> Won't it be affected by @cart changes? I would like to give it a try.

You should be able to get a working but probably inefficient solution to this using only `query.get`, which will should remain stable through the component storage changes that @cart is working on.

Stick to the public APIs for the proof of concept and I think it's safe to start on this @YohDeadfall :) If you can't get something working with public APIs only, then that's *also* useful information since it bumps the priority of this issue up quite a bit.

We're currently [discussing](https://discord.com/channels/691052431525675048/743663673393938453/818193044419117067) if this can be sensibly applied to accelerate iteration of UI hierarchies. A specialized UI storage type is the other alternative.

If we implemented IntoIter (see #1631) we could simply use [sorted_by_key](https://docs.rs/itertools/0.10.0/itertools/trait.Itertools.html#method.sorted_by_key) from iter_tools, possibly with a custom implementation for speed.

#1817 is a great stop-gap, but honestly I'm not content with the ergonomics here. This is a common and important operation, and it needs to be easy to write and read this pattern easily. The cost of mistakes is too high, and we may be able to optimize a dedicated method beyond `query::get`.
Ideally we'd be able to cache this order too, and somehow make this more efficient than `Query::get`.

@alice-i-cecile  it looks like perhaps this issue was closed mistakenly? I think that the changes in the commit referenced by bors add new methods for iterating over queries, but not for the kind of _ordered_ iteration you are proposing here? Apologies for the noise if I am mistaken! :-)
Nope, I agree with you. Reopening; I don't think the existing tools are enough.

## More use cases
- Rhythm games are an entire genre of games that would benefit from this addition.

## Implementation
The way I see it this could be done with 3 PRs.

### 1. Sorted Query Iteration
- Impl `Query::sorted_iter(self, key: fn(FilteredEntityRef) -> impl PartialOrd) -> SortedIter` + `mut` variant for sorted iteration.
- Sorts on first iteration or if change detection is triggered. Will not reorder tables but will build & maintain a `Vec` of `low..=high` ranges that is used for iteration. This `Vec` is cached for each `Query`. This is how flecs does this.
- The `low..=high` `Vec` could just be a field in `Query` or a `Component` with queries as entities.

### 2. API to swap entity positions in tables
- `World::swap(&mut self, e0: Entity, e1: Entity) -> SwapResult`. Tries to swap 2 entities in a table. If they do not belong to the same table nothing happens.

### 3. Table Sorting Command
- Impl a command to sort tables.
- Can be used in conjunction with sorted iteration.
- Reduces the memory footprint of the `low..=high` `Vec`.
- Reduces random access for sorted iteration making them more cache friendly.
- Being decoupled from queries removes performance foot guns:
    - Queries in systems requesting `mut` access to components for longer than they need to which would reduce the potential for parallelism.
    - Queries having similar but competing sorted ordering. Eg. system `foo` requesting sorted `&A`s but system `bar` requesting sorted `(&A, &B)`s.
- Use a stable sorting algorithm.
    - Results in more `low..=high` caches being condensed when users want different orderings in different systems on the same entities.
    
### Additionally:
Adding functionality for suspendable queries/caching iteration position allows expressing even more things at the level ECS with this feature. For instance UI could keep track of scroll position in a scroll area with this where the scroll area just uses Queries to get elements.

### Remaining work:
Query cache sharing. It will not be uncommon to have multiple systems that query for the same set of archetypes to want to iterate them in the same sorted order. This would result in doing the same sort multiple times to build the same order cache. Cache sharing would eliminate this.

> This is how flecs does this.

Not entirely correct, flecs does both:
- First a query makes sure all matching tables are sorted
- Then it builds a list of slices across tables so you get correct ordering across the query

Without step 1 you'd get way too many fragmented slices in step 2.

review_comments: I think that the fact this allocates a `Vec<_>` with all entities from the query is a drawback that should be mentioned
